paper.title: Pure Exploration in Kernel and Neural Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit pure exploration with adaptive embedding (misspecified linear representation)
unmapped: finite set of K arms in R^D with unknown reward function h: X -> [-1,1]
learner knows a family of feature maps psi_d: X -> R^d with h(x) = <psi_d(x), theta_d> + eta_d(x)
learner knows the misspecification level function gamma_tilde(d) bounding max_x |eta_d(x)|
gamma(d) assumed to vanish for d large enough
settings.definition_quote: Consider a set of arms $\cX \subseteq \R^D$ where the number of arms $\abs*{\cX} = K$ is possibly very large. We use an unknown function $h: \cX \rightarrow [-1,1]$ to represent the true reward of each arm. A noisy feedback $h(\bx) + \xi$ is observed after each sample arm $\bx$, where the noise $\xi$ is assumed to be $1$-sub-Gaussian. ... We assume the knowledge of both the feature mapping $\bpsi_d(\cdot)$ and the error function $\widetilde \gamma (\cdot)$.

unmapped: learner knows the Mercer eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the kernel
settings.definition_quote: We consider a kernel function $\cK: \cZ \times \cZ \rightarrow \R$ over a compact set $\cZ$ ... We assume $\cX \subseteq \cZ$ and the true reward of any arm $\bx \in \cX$ is given by an unknown function $h \in \cH$ such that $\norm{h}_{\cH} \leq 1$.

unmapped: NTK gram matrix over arms satisfies H >= lambda_0 I; learner needs lambda_0 to set network width m
arms have unit l2 norm with duplicated coordinates (j and j+d/2 identical)
finite arm set X of size K
settings.definition_quote: There exists $\lambda_0>0$ such that $\Hb \succeq \lambda_0 \Ib$. For any $\xb \in \cX$, the arm $\xb$ satisfies $\|\xb\|_2 = 1$ and that its $j$-th coordinate is identical to its $j+d/2$-th coordinate.

unmapped: learner knows a fixed feature map psi_d but NOT the misspecification level gamma_tilde(d)
unverifiable guarantee: algorithm starts outputting good arms but does not know when to stop
settings.definition_quote: We consider of version of \cref{alg:active_elim} with unknown mis-specification level $\widetilde \gamma(\cdot)$.

algorithms.name: Arm Elimination with Adaptive Embedding and Induced Misspecification (Algorithm 1)
Arm Elimination with Fixed Embedding and Induced Misspecification (Algorithm 3)
Arm Elimination with Fixed Embedding and Unknown Misspecification (Algorithm 4)

symbols.d_eff: effective dimension d_eff(epsilon) = min{d: gamma(d) <= epsilon} induced by the feature maps

conditions: gamma(d) can be made arbitrarily small for large d

source.label: thm:active_elim_adaptive
source.quote: With probability of at least $1-\delta$, \cref{alg:active_elim_adaptive} correctly outputs an $\epsilon$-optimal arm with sample complexity upper bounded by 640 \sum_{k=1}^{\ceil*{\log_2(2/\epsilon)}} ( ( k \, \rho_{d_k}^\star(2^{2-k}) \log(k^2 \abs{\cX}^2/\delta)) + (r_{d_k}(\zeta)+1) )= \widetilde{O} ( d_{\eff}(\epsilon) \cdot \max \{\Delta_{\min}, \epsilon\}^{-2} )

results.notes: The theorem also gives an exact instance-dependent sum 640*sum_k (k rho*_{d_k}(2^{2-k}) log(k^2 K^2/delta) + r_{d_k}(zeta)+1), not encoded as expression. Correctness: outputs epsilon-optimal arm w.p. >= 1-delta.

symbols.beta_decay: polynomial eigenvalue decay exponent: mu_j <= C_k j^{-beta}

source.label: thm:kernel_elim
source.quote: Suppose $\cK$ has $(C_k, \beta)$-polynomial eigenvalue decay. We have $d_{\eff}(\epsilon) = O \paren*{{\epsilon}^{-2/(2\beta -3)}}$, and the sample complexity of identifying an $\epsilon$-optimal arm is upper bounded by $\widetilde O ( \epsilon^{-2/(2\beta -3)} \max \curly*{\Delta_{\min}, \epsilon}^{-2} )$.

results.notes: High-probability (1-delta) via Theorem thm:active_elim_adaptive. Proof text states beta>3 in one place while assumption says beta>3/2.

source.label: thm:kernel_elim
source.quote: Suppose $\cK$ has $(C_k, \beta)$-exponential eigenvalue decay. We have $d_{\eff}(\epsilon) = O \paren*{\log(1/\epsilon)}$, and the sample complexity of identifying an $\epsilon$-optimal arm is upper bounded by $\widetilde O (\max \curly*{\Delta_{\min}, \epsilon}^{-2})$.

symbols.d_eff: neural effective dimension d_eff(bar_eps^2/|X|) = min{d: sum_{i>d} lambda_i(H) <= bar_eps^2/|X|} of the NTK gram matrix

conditions: Assumption 2: H >= lambda_0 I, ||x||_2 = 1 with symmetric coordinates, symmetric Gaussian initialization
network width m = poly(|X|, L, 1/lambda_0, log(|X|/delta_k), N_k, alpha, 1/bar_eps)
tuning: bar_eps^2 = min{alpha^2/(r_{|X|}^2(zeta) L), epsilon^2/((1+zeta)|X|S), epsilon^7 alpha^3/((1+zeta)^3|X|^3 log^3(|X|^2/delta_n) L^2)}
eta_k = C_1 (m alpha + N_k m L)^{-1}
J_k = log(C_2 eps^2 alpha/(N_k L))/(eta_k m L)

source.label: thm:neural
source.quote: then when $m = \text{poly}(|\cX|, L, \lambda_0^{-1}, \log(|\cX|/\delta_k), N_k, \alpha, \bar \epsilon^{-1})$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\widehat{\cS}_{n+1}$ only includes arm $\xb$ satisfying $\Delta_{\xb} \leq \epsilon$, and the total sample complexity of Algorithm \ref{alg:neural} is bounded by N = \widetilde O((1+\zeta)d_{\eff}(\bar \epsilon^2/|\cX|)/\epsilon^2 + r_{d_{\eff}(\bar \epsilon^2/|\cX|)}(\zeta) ) = \widetilde O(d_{\eff}(\bar \epsilon^2/|\cX|) \epsilon^{-2}).

results.notes: Formal version of informal Theorem 1 (thm:neural_inf), which states the same bound. S here is the bound on sqrt(h^T H^-1 h).

symbols.rho_d: instance complexity rho*_d(gamma(d)) = inf_lambda sup_x ||psi_d(x*)-psi_d(x)||^2_{A(lambda)^-1}/max{Delta_x, gamma(d)}^2
symbols.r_d: number of samples r_d(zeta) required by the rounding procedure in R^d

source.label: thm:active_elim
source.quote: With probability of at least $1-\delta$, \cref{alg:active_elim} correctly outputs an $\gamma (d)$-optimal arm with sample complexity upper bounded by N \leq 640 \, \rho_d^\star(\gamma(d)) \log_2 (\frac{4}{ \gamma(d)}) \log ( \frac{\log_2 (4/ \gamma(d)) \abs{\cX}^2 }{\delta} ) + (r_d(\zeta) + 1) \log_2 (\frac{4}{ \gamma(d)}).

results.notes: Guarantee is for identifying a gamma(d)-optimal arm (with d = d_eff(epsilon) this is epsilon-optimal, Remark 6).

symbols.n_d: critical number of iterations n(d) up to which misspecification error is controlled

conditions: gamma_tilde(d) > 0 and unknown to the learner

source.label: thm:active_elim_unknown
source.quote: Suppose $\widetilde \gamma(d)$ is unknown. With probability of at least $1-\delta$, \cref{alg:active_elim_unknown} starts to output a $\overline  \gamma(d)$-optimal arm after at most $N$ samples where N \leq 640 \, \rho^\star(\overline \gamma(d)) \log_2 (n(d)) \log ( \frac{(n(d) \abs{\cX})^2 }{\delta} ) + (r(\zeta) + 1) \, n(d).

results.notes: Unverifiable sample complexity: the algorithm starts outputting gamma_bar(d)-optimal arms after N samples but does not know when to stop. gamma_bar(d) <= gamma(d) by Proposition prop:round_and_error.

cited_results.setting_description: Best-arm identification (fixed confidence) in linear bandits in R^d without misspecification; lower bound in terms of rho_tilde*(0)
